findings.title: End-to-end NetSuite verification still outstanding
findings.description: Plan §4 flags the sandbox host rule (1234567_SB1 -> 1234567-sb1) and the overall flow as asserted but not verified against live NetSuite. Unit tests cover the documented rule, but the §5 manual/smoke acceptance items (function appears in autocomplete; a real bearer token works against a sandbox) are not demonstrable from the diff.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm the token flow end-to-end against a NetSuite sandbox before merge, or explicitly defer it as a tracked follow-up. No code change required.

findings.title: Toast classification keys off err.name rather than instanceof
findings.description: onRender uses err.name === 'TokenExchangeError' to choose specific-vs-generic message. This is intentionally bundling-robust (constructor sets this.name to a literal that survives esbuild minification, where instanceof against the class identifier can be fragile), but the intent is not documented.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a one-line comment explaining why err.name is checked instead of instanceof TokenExchangeError, so a future reader does not 'fix' it.

findings.title: expiresIn silently falls back to assertion TTL on missing/non-numeric value
findings.description: When expires_in is absent or non-numeric, exchangeToken defaults to ASSERTION_TTL_SECONDS (3600). NetSuite always returns expires_in, so a response without it is arguably malformed and better treated as an error than cached for an hour.
findings.recommended_fix: Optionally treat a missing/non-numeric expires_in as a TokenExchangeError rather than defaulting to 3600. Low priority hardening.
